ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, an object m is placed on an inclined plane body of mass M, and m can slide down along the inclined plane body at a uniform speed. Now a force F along the inclined plane downward is used to push the object, making it move down along the inclined plane with uniform acceleration. Question: Does the horizontal ground exert a frictional force on the inclined plane body?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is an inclined plane body M placed on horizontal ground, with the inclined plane sloping upward to the right; a small block m is placed on the inclined plane; near the block, an external force F along the direction of the inclined plane is drawn. The problem statement says that this force F pushes the object downward along the inclined plane. Let the inclination angle of the inclined plane be θ. Reasoning: When F is not applied, the block m can slide down along the inclined plane body at a uniform speed, indicating that the resultant force on the block along the direction of the inclined plane is zero. At this time, the component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sinθ, and the kinetic friction force is upward along the inclined plane, with magnitude f=μN; in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane, N=mg cosθ. Therefore mg sinθ=f=μmg cosθ, that is, μ=tanθ. After adding the force F downward along the inclined plane, F has no component in the direction perpendicular to the inclined plane, so the normal pressure of the block on the inclined plane is still N=mg cosθ; since the block still slides down along the inclined plane, the magnitude of the friction force is still f=μN=mg sinθ. F only changes the acceleration of the block along the direction of the inclined plane, and does not change the normal pressure or the magnitude of the friction force. Look at the action exerted by the block on the inclined plane body M in the horizontal direction: the magnitude of the horizontal component of the pressure of the block on the inclined plane body is N sinθ, and its direction is opposite to the horizontal component f cosθ of the friction force of the block on the inclined plane body. Substituting N=mg cosθ and f=mg sinθ gives N sinθ=mg cosθ sinθ and f cosθ=mg sinθ cosθ; the two are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, so the horizontal resultant force exerted by the block on the inclined plane body is zero. Therefore, the horizontal ground does not need to provide a frictional force on the inclined plane body.
